Propagate reproduction-matrix uncertainty to outbreak risk

Source: R/inference.R
estimate_rob.Rd

Draws complete reproduction matrices from a fitted Gamma posterior and applies outbreak_prob(), r_ob(), and optionally r_ref() to every draw. The transmission likelihood is Poisson; negative-binomial transmission inference is not implied by the offspring-distribution option in outbreak_prob(). Intervals are posterior credible intervals, not frequentist bootstrap intervals.

Usage

estimate_rob(
  fit,
  draws = 1000,
  seed = NULL,
  level = 0.95,
  return_draws = FALSE,
  include_rref = TRUE,
  max_fail_fraction = 0.05,
  tol = 1e-12,
  max_iter = 1e+05
)

Arguments

fit

An object returned by infer_R() or infer_R_sufficient().

draws

Positive integer number of posterior matrices to sample.

seed

Optional finite integer random seed.

level

Credible interval level strictly between zero and one.

return_draws

If TRUE, include posterior matrix, outbreak-ratio, and outbreak-probability draws in the returned object.

include_rref

If TRUE, calculate the reference reproduction ratio for every successful draw.

max_fail_fraction

Maximum tolerated fraction of failed draws.

tol, max_iter

Numerical controls passed to outbreak_prob().

Value

An object of class routbreak_rob_estimate. Its summary data frame contains posterior medians and lower/upper credible limits for R_ob, outbreak probability, and (when requested) R_ref. requested_draws, successful_draws, failed_draws, failures, and diagnostics report the failure fraction, reasons, numerical controls, and Gamma-underflow replacements. If return_draws = TRUE, successful matrix, R_ob, outbreak-probability, and optional R_ref draws are returned in arrays or matrices preserving community identifiers.

Details

Draws that fail numerical or theoretical checks are recorded. Any failures produce a warning, and the function errors when their fraction exceeds max_fail_fraction. R's Gamma generator can underflow to exact zero for very small shape parameters even though a proper Gamma distribution has strictly positive support. Such values are replaced by the smallest positive normalized floating-point value and counted in the diagnostics; this prevents numerical underflow from creating artificial structural zeros.

Posterior draws are independent Gamma samples, not an MCMC chain, so MCMC convergence diagnostics do not apply. Reported quantiles still have Monte Carlo error; users should increase draws and check stability for final analyses. If some draws fail within the allowed fraction, summaries are conditional on the successful draws and must be interpreted with the accompanying failure diagnostics.

Examples

S <- matrix(12, 1, 1, dimnames = list("A", "A"))
fit <- infer_R_sufficient(
  S, E = c(A = 10), prior_shape = 1, prior_rate = 1
)
estimate <- estimate_rob(fit, draws = 20, seed = 1)
estimate$summary
#>   community R_ob_median R_ob_lower R_ob_upper outbreak_probability_median
#> A         A    1.216999  0.6383935   1.593597                   0.3297678
#>   outbreak_probability_lower outbreak_probability_upper R_ref_median
#> A                          0                  0.6384559     1.216999
#>   R_ref_lower R_ref_upper
#> A   0.6383935    1.593597
estimate$diagnostics
#> $tolerance
#> [1] 1e-12
#> 
#> $max_iterations
#> [1] 100000
#> 
#> $failure_fraction
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $gamma_underflow_replacements
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $convergence
#> [1] "Every successful draw satisfied the fixed-point residual check implemented by outbreak_prob()."
#>
